standard.title: Interpret and convey meaning in the target language
standard.description: develop and begin to apply strategies to interpret, translate and convey meaning in the target language in familiar contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate and process information in familiar target language texts (AC9LS8EC04). They have not yet developed or applied explicit strategies for interpreting, translating or conveying meaning between languages — these skills are emerging and require explicit scaffolding at this entry point.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop and begin to apply a set of interpretation and translation strategies for familiar contexts, including using dictionaries, recognising cognates and false friends, inferring from context, and understanding that translation involves more than word-for-word equivalence.

nodes.label: Using dictionaries and reference tools
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use print and online dictionaries to assist with interpreting and translating familiar target language words and short phrases.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a dictionary (print or digital) to look up at least five unfamiliar words and check the result in context.
nodes.typical_width: Use dictionaries and reference tools to assist with translation and interpretation tasks; recognise that dictionary entries give multiple possible meanings and that context determines the right choice; develop habits of cross-checking.
wider: Compare results from multiple translation tools (dictionary, online translator, peer) for the same text — evaluate which is most accurate for a given context and explain why
Identify one case where a direct dictionary translation produces an inaccurate or awkward result — explain what additional knowledge is needed
nodes.hinge_reason: Without functional dictionary use, students cannot independently interpret unfamiliar language — they are entirely dependent on teacher-provided glossaries. This limits access to the wider text encounters that develop interpretation strategies in nodes 2–4.

response_modes.reason: Dictionary use is a procedural skill — looking up, choosing between multiple entries, checking in context. Reliable use requires practice across varied word types and contexts until the habit is automatic.

success_criteria: Can use a dictionary to locate the meaning of an unfamiliar word and select the contextually appropriate definition
Can identify when a dictionary definition does not fit the context and attempt an alternative interpretation

nodes.label: Recognising cognates and false friends
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify cognate patterns between the target language and English as a meaning-prediction strategy, and recognise that 'false friends' exist.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three cognates between the target language and English and use them to predict meaning in a text; identify at least one example of a false friend.
nodes.typical_width: Use cognate recognition as a systematic strategy for predicting meaning in unfamiliar texts; build awareness of false friend patterns; recognise that cognate reliability varies across target languages.
wider: Investigate cognate patterns systematically — e.g. common suffix or prefix patterns that reliably predict meaning in the target language — and create a class reference resource
Research the historical or linguistic reasons why a known false friend diverged in meaning between the target language and English

response_modes.reason: Cognate recognition as a strategy requires exposure to enough examples for the pattern to become intuitive. Students need to encounter cognates across multiple text types before they will apply the strategy spontaneously rather than only when prompted.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cognate pattern awareness is a transferable metalinguistic skill — it accelerates vocabulary acquisition not just in this target language but in any related language the student encounters. The investment compounds across the secondary sequence.
success_criteria: Can identify at least three cognates between the target language and English and use them to successfully predict meaning in a new text
Can identify at least one false friend and explain why it is misleading

nodes.label: Inferring meaning from context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use contextual cues (surrounding text, visual elements, known vocabulary) to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least one successful inference from context in a target language text — explain what cues they used.
nodes.typical_width: Apply a range of inferencing strategies (known vocabulary, grammatical patterns, visual context, topic knowledge) to unfamiliar words and expressions in target language texts; distinguish between high-confidence and low-confidence inferences.
wider: Observe target language interactions (recorded or live) and identify how non-verbal and contextual cues support meaning-making where linguistic knowledge is incomplete
Compare inferencing strategies with a peer — identify where different prior knowledge leads to different inferences from the same text

response_modes.reason: Inferencing is a strategy that must be made explicit before students will apply it independently. Think-aloud modelling of the inferencing process — 'I don't know this word, but I can see that... and the topic is... so it probably means...' — builds the reasoning habit.

success_criteria: Can make at least one successful inference about an unfamiliar word using contextual cues and explain the reasoning
Can identify the type of cue used (surrounding words, visual, topic knowledge) for each inference attempt

nodes.label: Understanding that translation involves more than word equivalence
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that direct word-for-word translation does not always convey accurate meaning, and can explain at least one reason why.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one expression or phrase in the target language that does not translate word-for-word into English; explain what additional knowledge is needed.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise the distinction between literal and non-literal translation; identify idioms, fixed expressions and abbreviated forms that require interpretation beyond word equivalence; understand that abbreviations, slang and digital communication conventions vary between languages.
wider: Analyse an automated translation of a familiar text — identify specific errors or awkward renderings and explain what the tool missed
Translate a short familiar English text into the target language and compare it with a classmate's or automated version — discuss where choices diverged and why

response_modes.reason: Understanding translation as interpretation rather than substitution draws on all prior nodes — dictionary use, cognate awareness, contextual inferencing — and adds the conceptual insight that meaning is shaped by culture and context, not only by language structure. This prepares students for EC05's Y9-10 demands.

success_criteria: Can identify at least one expression in the target language that cannot be translated word-for-word and explain why
Can evaluate an automated or peer translation of a short text and identify at least one improvement
